newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan February bad-cheque ratio rises to 0.60 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan February bad-cheque ratio rises to 0.60 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's bad-cheque ratio was at 0.60 percent in February, up from January's 0.55 percent, the local Commercial Times newspaper reported on Sunday.

The number of bad cheques accounted for 0.60 percent of the total cheques written in Februay, with a value representing 0.36 percent of the value of all cheques written, the paper quoted the central bank as saying.
The monthly bad-cheque ratio hit a 10-year high of 0.80 percent in October 1995, the central bank said.
In annual terms, 1995's 0.67 percent was also a 10-year peak, the highest since the ratio hit 0.75 percent in 1985.

The bank attributed the rising number of bad cheques in 1995 to the slow economy and Taiwan's slumping property and stock markets. But in recent months, the bad-cheque problems have eased gradually, it said.
